elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 (retained, unedited): "Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 warrants Services and Deliverables will "materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications"; edited § 19.2 covers "each Deliverable and software delivered to Customer will materially conform to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Edited § 19.2 sets the conformance period at "ninety (90) days after delivery", and expressly states Vendor has no correction or refund obligation after that date — short of the 12-month preferred period.
§ 19.1's Services warranties carry no expiry, and the § 19.2 cut-off is limited to Deliverables and delivered software; an unlimited Services warranty exceeds 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: § 19.4: "Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."
§ 19.4: "Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the rendered § 19.1–19.4 language or the cited paragraphs; § 19.3 was not reproduced, so its content cannot be confirmed.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: Per the finding's own rationale, § 19.3 limits malicious-code cover to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", which is narrower than an unqualified no-malicious-code warranty, and the redline does not repair it.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 rewrites § 19.2 to read "For ninety (90) days after delivery, each Deliverable and software delivered to Customer will materially conform to its documentation" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at the 90-day floor (deterministic period check passed).

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 warrants Services performance and Services conformance with no stated expiry; the § 19.2 time bar reaches only Deliverables and delivered software, so the Services warranty runs longer than 30 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: § 19.4 (unchanged, and cross-referring to §§ 19.1 and 19.2): "promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."
§ 19.4 second sentence gives Customer termination of the affected item plus "a refund of Fees paid for it" if cure fails within a reasonable period.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: the single edit lifts § 19.2 from fifteen to ninety (90) days and expressly extends it to "software delivered to Customer", while the pre-existing § 19.4 repair/replace and refund remedies (which cross-refer to § 19.2) are untouched.

Preferred level fails on three elements: the software conformance period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the malicious-code warranty in § 19.3 remains narrowed to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", and no compliance-with-applicable-laws warranty is visible in the rendered or cited language. To reach preferred the drafter would need to state "for twelve (12) months after delivery" in § 19.2, strike "intentionally introduced by Vendor" from § 19.3, and insert an express Vendor warranty of compliance with applicable laws.

Minimality holds: only the numeral and the software scope words in § 19.2 changed. The added phrase is necessary because "Deliverable" is defined as reports, configurations, specifications and similar work product and excludes Vendor Technology, so without it there would be no express software-to-documentation warranty; no survival tails, expense language, procedures or extra remedies were added, and the Customer-unfavourable but pre-existing sunset sentence was correctly left in place rather than deleted.

Intent is preserved: § 19.4's remedy cascade, the non-exclusivity carve-out for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims, and § 19.1's undated Services warranties all survive without contradiction, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling.

Note for the record: hosted software supplied as a Service may not literally be "delivered" to Customer; if the reviewing team wants the SaaS layer squarely inside § 19.2, consider "each Deliverable and any software delivered or made available to Customer". This is a refinement, not a fallback gap, since § 19.1's undated conformance warranty already reaches Services.
